draft.title: Compound interest
card: With compound interest, the interest earned is added to the balance. The next period's interest is then worked out on the larger amount. So interest earns interest.
The formula is A = P(1 + r)ⁿ. A is the final amount, P is the amount invested at the start, r is the rate per period as a decimal, and n is the number of periods.
Rate and periods must match. For 6% per year compounded monthly, r = 0.06 ÷ 12 = 0.005 and n is the number of months.
Example: $2000 at 5% per year for 3 years. A = 2000 × 1.05³ = 2000 × 1.157625 = $2315.25. The interest earned is $315.25.
draft.remember: Multiply by (1 + r) once for each period. Match r and n to the same period.

a.q: Mia invests $1000 at 10% per year, compounded yearly, for 2 years. What is the final amount?
a.why: A = 1000 × 1.1² = 1000 × 1.21 = $1210. The answer $1200 is simple interest, which does not let the interest earn interest.
a.clue: Multiply by 1.1 once for each year.

b.q: Sam invests $5000 at 6% per year, compounded monthly, for 2 years. Which calculation gives the final amount?
b.why: The rate per month is 0.06 ÷ 12 = 0.005, and there are 2 × 12 = 24 months. So A = 5000 × 1.005²⁴. Using 1.06² ignores the monthly compounding, so it does not match the period.
b.clue: Convert both the rate and the time to months.

problems.detail: The clue 'Multiply by 1.1 once for each year' gives the student the whole method (1000 × 1.1 × 1.1), so the question no longer tests whether they can set up compound interest, only the arithmetic.
